html:
A cloth woven on narrow looms in strips of silk and cotton by Asante weavers around Bonwire near Kumasi and by Ewe weavers in the Volta region, then sewn into large wraps.

Once reserved for Asante royalty and great occasions, each pattern has a name and meaning. Silk thread first came from unravelled European cloth bought on the coast. Nkrumah wore kente at independence and on visits abroad, and it became a symbol of African pride; in the United States it is worn at graduations. Kente is now made and printed across the world. See also Akan art.
